subject: awaitEvent (internal/core/machine/await_test.go), the bounded wait every test of the package uses for an event the code under test must produce (#935)
why: A bare receive on such an event turns a guard that refuses early into a hang until the package timeout, and a falsify verdict cut short that way reads like a mutation with fewer catchers. awaitEvent asks three questions of a wait: did the event come, did it come before the deadline given, and if not, does the failure say what did not happen; one mutation per question, the first two both striking the deadline (unreachable, then early). awaitEventBefore adds three: did the subject return before the event, does the failure then carry the subject's error, and does an event that came win over a return that followed it; one mutation each, and a fourth for a nil return before the event. And one proving a race test does not lean on the helper alone: the subject produced the event, then returned nil without the step. And one on a call site, to show a real early refusal now fails at once with its cause instead of hanging. awaitWaitGroup (#963) asks two: does it give up at the deadline on a goroutine that never finishes, and does it wait for the goroutines that do finish; one mutation each. And one on a call site, a product deadlock, to show a subject that never releases now fails in about five seconds with a reason instead of hanging the package. Cycle 1 of #963 adds three helpers and two bounds. awaitReturn runs the second operation of a race test, which used to run unbounded on the test's own goroutine; it asks two questions, does it give up at the deadline and does it hand back the operation's error, one mutation each, and one on a call site, a lock the first operation never releases. goroutineErrors, in the machine package and in its copy in the Outscale pack, asks one, does report lose what was collected; one mutation per copy. And the request clients of the Outscale and emulator tests gained a timeout, the only bound of a request made from the test's own goroutine; one mutation per client. Cycle 2: the two client bounds are asserted on the clients the tests use and the give-up is played on a 50 ms client, one mutation per question; the attribution barrier is a channel a cleanup can open, one mutation for the abort and one for the wait on the partner. Cycle 3 (2026-11-16): the request clients and the waits on a request's answer get their own bound, requestTimeout (60 s), apart from subjectDeadline, after a legitimate 7.2 s round-trip failed main on macos-15-intel; one mutation per package puts awaitAnswer back on subjectDeadline.

mutations.label: awaitWaitGroup loses its deadline in effect: the wait is armed for a million times what the caller gave, so a goroutine that never finishes holds the test for fourteen hours, which is the bare wg.Wait() this issue replaces. The 20 s timeout makes that hang read HUNG, never a bite

awaitWaitGroup stops waiting: its goroutine closes done without wg.Wait(), so the helper returns while the subject still runs and every assertion after it reads a result not yet written. The refusing test above also goes red (no failure is reported), but the accepting test is the one that names the defect: it counts the goroutines that had finished when the helper returned

a call site, end to end: Binding.Serialise takes the target's lock and hands back a release that does nothing, so the second of eight actions on one target waits forever, a deadlock in the subject. The test now fails on awaitWaitGroup naming what did not finish; the 30 s timeout makes a hang read HUNG, so a bite here means the test went red inside 30 s. Measured by hand on 2026-11-15 in a copy (go test -overlay, -race, -timeout 30s): with awaitWaitGroup, FAIL TestSerialiseExcludesTwoActionsOnOneTarget (5.00s); with main 3a45c83's bare wg.Wait(), `panic: test timed out after 30s`

a call site, end to end, on the second operation of a race test: IsolateNetwork takes the network's lock and never gives it back, so the RemoveNetwork that follows waits forever. The 30 s timeout makes a hang read HUNG, so a bite means red inside 30 s.
